solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strand House cook claimed by horrendous death peril

indicators.note: something claimed by another is taken into it, so the cooking word sits inside the shuffled letters
something horrendous is a mess, so the letters of death peril are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to cook something is to heat it

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a cook in some building has been seized by a terrible threat of death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrendous' turns DEATH PERIL into ADELPHITRE, and 'claimed by' puts HEAT inside it after the T. The Strand is a famous London street of theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adelphi is a long-running West End playhouse standing on the Strand in London.

clue.text: Right among it, Dawkins heartlessly slammed Huxley?

indicators.note: one thing placed among others goes into their midst, here the right-hand letter
words that are slammed are knocked about, so the letters are rearranged
without its heart, the central letter of the name Dawkins is removed

explanation.surface: Richard Dawkins, a modern evolutionist, is pictured cruelly attacking the Victorian biologist Thomas Huxley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the central K; 'slammed' rearranges the rest with IT into DAWINIST, and 'among' sets R inside. The question mark marks Huxley as one example of an evolution champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Henry Huxley was the great champion of evolution by natural selection, nicknamed Darwin's Bulldog.

clue.text: Girl left in Douala after evacuation

indicators.note: a town emptied by evacuation keeps only its outer letters, the inside being cleared out

explanation.surface: A young woman has stayed behind in Douala, the Cameroonian port, after everyone else was evacuated.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Adapting to an Irish Herodotus?

indicators.note: adapting something alters its form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an ancient Greek writer could be adapted for an Irish audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Herodotus is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus, called the Father of History, wrote the earliest surviving Greek chronicle of the past.

clue.text: Two-wheeler parked in Clifton Gardens

indicators.note: something parked in a place sits within it, so the letters lie inside these two words

explanation.surface: A bicycle has been left in some gardens in Clifton, a district of Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light horse-drawn two-wheeled carriage used in India.

clue.text: City journalist at home gets hot food served up

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword's standard journalist
someone at home is in

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer working from home has a hot meal brought to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses H and GRUB to give BURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: All fingers and thumbs — or finding settled course

parts.note: eight fingers and two thumbs add up to ten

explanation.surface: A clumsy person asks whether they will ever find their way through a set path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' usually means clumsy; here it is a count.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of something is its general drift or steady direction, as in the even tenor of life.

clue.text: Stylish top from Ellesse on six- footer

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an insect has six feet, and an ant is the crossword's usual one

explanation.surface: A fashionable top from the sportswear brand Ellesse is worn by a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, which is what stylish describes.

clue.text: Count on this as Cuba undergoes reform

indicators.note: something reformed is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political commentator says you can count on Cuba going through reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on this' reads as 'depend on it' but means a thing you count with.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads slid along wires is a traditional calculating device used for counting.

clue.text: Times introduction to Romanticism about George Gordon

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper prints an introduction to Romantic poetry concerning a particular George Gordon.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gordon was the given name of the Romantic poet Lord Byron.

clue.text: One entering judgement shows awareness

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a court's sentence is its judgement on the guilty
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A judge passing judgement shows that they understand the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, which is a kind of consciousness.

clue.text: Windy City an effort with cold greeting Charlie

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hi is an informal greeting
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a go is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: Someone makes an attempt to say hello to Charlie while suffering from a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windy City is the long-standing nickname of the largest city in Illinois.

clue.text: Late bar vibrant in province

indicators.note: something vibrant is lively and in motion, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A late-opening bar is full of life somewhere in a province.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of the Canadian provinces, home to Calgary and Edmonton.

clue.text: European wife is aboard steamer

indicators.note: being aboard a ship means being inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A man notes that his wife from the Continent is on board a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Switzerland is one kind of European.

clue.text: Money given by sons relaxing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons
chilling is slang for relaxing

explanation.surface: Some cash has been handed out by sons who are taking it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was the currency of Austria before the euro.

clue.text: Eminent MP men flog during sex

indicators.note: things happening during something fall inside it

parts.note: it is an old euphemism for sex
taken as written: Member of Parliament
OR, other ranks, means men in the army
to tan someone's hide is to flog them

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: a politician and others whipping people in the middle of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords, men are the other ranks (OR) of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone important is a person of high standing or note.

clue.text: Dad with receding hair at party greets initially wild creature

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the letters of hair are read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter

explanation.surface: A balding father at a party says hello to something untamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receding hair' looks like baldness but reverses HAIR to give RIAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah dog is a half-wild ownerless dog that scavenges around villages in Asia.

clue.text: Shooter Ann flees wounded catamountain

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged, so the letters left are reworked

parts.note: taken as written: an old word for a wild cat

explanation.surface: A woman with a gun runs away from the wild cat she has injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flees' takes the letters of ANN out of CATAMOUNTAIN, and 'wounded' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic is a self-loading firearm, the kind of gun that could be called a shooter.

clue.text: Earl, King and Queen around Hampshire river

indicators.note: the outer pieces go around the river's name

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
the Itchen is a chalk stream flowing through Winchester and Southampton

explanation.surface: A noble and the royal couple stand beside a river in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Kitchener, the field marshal of the Great War recruiting poster, was made an earl.

clue.text: Boat, in erect position, that's in bottle

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
standing upright means being up

explanation.surface: A boat stands upright inside a bottle, like a model ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ship in a bottle; the bottle actually holds a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato sauce is usually sold and served from a bottle on the table.

clue.text: Yank walloped companion

parts.note: to wallop someone is to hit them
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: An American has struck his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is a verb, to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch something is to pull or jerk it up sharply.

clue.text: Troika ultimately leaves country empty

indicators.note: a letter that leaves a word is taken out of it

parts.note: Hungary is a central European country

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letter

explanation.surface: A three-person ruling group finally quits, leaving the nation empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling empty is a common way to describe being in need of food.

clue.text: Restraint needed after cutting sweet pastry

indicators.note: one piece needed after another follows it

parts.note: a cutting remark is a tart one
let is an old word for hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Holding back is necessary after slicing a pastry dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: LET as a hindrance survives in tennis and in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open pie with a sweet filling is a little pastry case or tart.

clue.text: Little jumper worn by Neo's lover

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone surrounds them, so the wearer goes inside

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a jumping animal
Neo is the setter's name, so the setter means me

explanation.surface: The setter's sweetheart is wearing a small sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is a British word for a sweater, misdirecting from the kangaroo; the setter refers to themself by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is Shakespeare's young lover, and the name stands for any ardent suitor.

clue.text: African expresses disapproval over island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: someone who tuts makes a clicking sound of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa frowns on something happening on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Belly beginning to bulge — notice old chaps holding that in!

indicators.note: something holding another contains it

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Elderly men, spotting a paunch starting to show, suck their stomachs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' refers back to the first letter of bulge, which goes inside AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the everyday word for the front of the body between chest and hips.

clue.text: Play a measure first

indicators.note: the measure comes first, ahead of the single letter

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

explanation.surface: An instruction to play one bar of music before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a drama is a work written for the stage and performed by actors.

clue.text: Clumsy punch cuts boxer Naz

indicators.note: a piece that cuts another goes into it

parts.note: Prince Naseem Hamed was a British featherweight champion known as Naz
a fist is a punch, as in to make a fist at

explanation.surface: A blow opens a cut on a boxer during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-fisted means awkward with the hands, much like butterfingered or bungling.

clue.text: Daisy's teacher docking marks

indicators.note: docking means cutting off, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A teacher called Daisy takes marks off pupils' work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marks' suggests school grades but is the German currency, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a plant of the daisy family with star-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Plato, in McHugh novel, takes in grand field event

indicators.note: something that takes in another holds it inside
novel means new, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Plato features in a novel by someone called McHugh, which takes in a large sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the fodder across the surface's phrase: 'novel' shuffles all three words, and 'takes in' puts the grand inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploughing match is a farming contest held in a field to see who ploughs the straightest furrows.
